name: Nuoc mot
summary: A lightly sweet herb drink, cold after a hot walk or hot in the wet months, usually carried away in the hand. The herbs vary by maker: monk fruit and licorice with ginger, lemongrass, cinnamon, lemon, green tea, and chamomile, or with chrysanthemum and lotus leaf.
origin: Hoi An, where it is called nước mót or trà Mót.
taste: Lightly sweet. One maker steeps ginger, lemongrass, cinnamon, licorice, lemon, green tea, chamomile, and monk fruit.
Another steeps monk fruit, licorice, chrysanthemum, and lotus leaf.
howToEat: A cold cup after a hot walk, or a hot cup in the wet months, usually taken away in the hand.
where: The old town, in the hand.
seoTitle: Nuoc mot — Hoi An herb drink
seoDescription: Nước mót is Hoi An’s lightly sweet herb drink, cold after a hot walk or hot in the wet months.
